name: Djondb
tagline: Abandoned C++ document database that paired schema-free JSON documents with multi-document transactions.
description: Djondb was an open-source document database written in C++ by Juan Pablo Crossley and launched around 2012. It stored JSON/BSON documents in schema-free namespaces and set itself apart from early MongoDB by focusing on consistency and transactions that span several documents, with a command shell plus drivers for Java, C#, Node.js, PHP, Python and Go. The engine was GPL-licensed with a commercial licence offered to OEMs. Driver work continued into 2017 (the npm client reached 3.5.x), after which the project stopped and djondb.com became a parked domain. Anyone wanting transactional documents today has MongoDB, Couchbase or PostgreSQL JSONB.
statusNote: Abandoned around 2017; djondb.com is now a parked domain and only mirrors of the source remain. Use MongoDB, Couchbase or PostgreSQL JSONB instead.

license.name: GNU GPL v2 (commercial licence also offered)

pricing.notes: GPL for open-source use; the commercial OEM licence and enterprise subscription are no longer offered.

strengths: Aimed at multi-document transactions years before MongoDB offered them
Native C++ engine with drivers for six languages
Small codebase that is easy to read for students of document stores
weaknesses: Dead since 2017: no site, docs or maintained builds
Original repository is gone; only third-party mirrors exist
Never documented a replication or sharding story
useCases: Historical reference on early transactional document stores
Reading a compact C++ BSON storage implementation
